features.name: Excel report layouts
features.description: Built-in functionality in Business Central that allows users to create Excel-based report layouts from any existing report data set without coding experience. Enables interactive data analysis with pivot tables, filters, conditional formatting, and advanced Excel capabilities.
caveats: Not designed primarily for printing
Requires user understanding of Excel to maximize capabilities
Data contract must start at cell A1
Cannot modify column names in data sheet
System sheets typically hidden by default

features.name: Power Query integration for refreshable reports
features.description: Ability to combine data from multiple sources including Business Central and external databases using Power Query within Excel reports. Enables refreshable, real-time reporting scenarios using APIs and environmental variables.
caveats: Requires custom APIs for some scenarios
More complex than basic Excel reports
Company ID may contain curly brackets requiring data cleanup

features.name: Data contract in Excel layouts
features.description: The data sheet containing field names from the report data set that tie back to Business Central. Must include at least one column, must start at cell A1, and cannot be modified except by developers adding new columns.
caveats: Must not be modified by end users
Must start at cell A1
Can only include columns in the report data set

features.name: System Excel sheets and metadata
features.description: Hidden system sheets that provide metadata about reports including report AL metadata, request metadata, request page filters, caption data, translation data, and aggregated metadata. Contains information about tenant, environment, company, and language settings.
caveats: Hidden by default
Not intended for end user modification
Can be hidden but cannot be secured from users

features.name: Named formulas for metadata access
features.description: Pre-built XLOOKUPs in Excel that allow easy access to aggregated metadata such as company ID, environment name, and tenant entry ID without typing out complex formulas.

features.name: Excel native features in report layouts
features.description: Support for using Excel's built-in features such as grouping, subtotals, conditional formatting, removing duplicates, and analysis tools within Excel report layouts to post-process data from Business Central.

features.name: Copilot integration in Excel reports
features.description: Ability to use Copilot within Excel to analyze data from Business Central reports, look at trends, leverage KPIs, and perform forecasting or what-if analysis.

features.name: OneDrive integration for Excel reports
features.description: Administrator setup wizard to integrate OneDrive with Business Central, allowing Excel reports to be stored in cloud-shared locations rather than downloaded to user computers. Enables comments, sharing, and data protection features. When OneDrive is configured, the workbook downloads to OneDrive and opens in browser; otherwise it downloads to the user's device.
caveats: Popups must not be blocked
External sharing settings in SharePoint must be reviewed

features.name: Physical inventory Excel reports
features.description: Physical inventory list report exported to Excel with quantity calculated and item tracking numbers, allowing users to filter by location or item and work easily in Excel instead of printing. Can be customized to import results back into Business Central journals.
caveats: Customization may be needed for import back into Business Central

features.name: Multilingual Excel report layouts
features.description: Support for translation data and caption mapping that allows Excel report layouts to automatically display in the user's language at runtime. Uses translation data which leverages the user's language to translate strings that don't exist as captions in the report object.

features.name: Office 365 collaboration for Excel reports
features.description: Excel reports can be stored in SharePoint and leveraged with Office 365 suite features, enabling real-time collaboration on Excel reports with co-workers.

features.name: Excel layout import and validation
features.description: Users can import Excel layout files back into Business Central after design and formula work. The system validates that the Excel file is not password protected, the data worksheet exists with correct naming, and columns in the data contract are validated on import.
caveats: Excel file cannot be password protected
Data worksheet must exist and be properly named
Columns are validated against data contract
System may fail or get confused during processing if data is present

features.name: Excel report layout testing and execution
features.description: Users select an Excel layout from the report layout screen and run it. If OneDrive is configured, the workbook downloads to OneDrive and opens in browser; otherwise it downloads to the user's device. The server generates the dataset, applies filters and options, loads the Excel layout file, and inserts data into the data contract.
caveats: Data mapping must be correct when loading into data contract

features.name: Refreshable Excel report layouts
features.description: Refreshable Excel report layouts use APIs and Power Query to create a connection back to Business Central. Users can open Excel and refresh data to pull current information from Business Central without re-running the report. Business Central provides environment information via aggregated metadata sheet.

features.name: Business Central API structure and authentication
features.description: APIs follow a standard structure: API.Central.dynamics.com/2.0/[tenant-id]/[environment-name]/api/[publisher]/[group]/[API]. Users connect via OData feed in Excel Power Query using organizational account authentication. Out-of-the-box APIs like sales orders do not require publisher name and API group; these are only needed for custom APIs.
caveats: Requires organizational account sign-in
May reprompt for connection authentication

features.name: Dynamic API connection using environment variables
features.description: Users can build dynamic API connections in Power Query using variables that extract environment information from the aggregated metadata sheet (tenant ID, environment name, company ID). This allows easy switching between sandbox and production environments by reading report request parameters.
caveats: Company ID may contain curly brackets requiring data cleanup

features.name: Custom APIs for Excel reports
features.description: Users can build Excel reports using custom APIs created for specific business purposes. Example shown is a custom API for sales order item categories with publisher and API group designation that can be called from Power Query.

features.name: Permissions and API access for Excel reports
features.description: Excel reports using APIs require users to have read permissions on tables used in the report. When connecting via API, users must have table permissions configured.

features.name: Sheet protection and password limitations
features.description: Sheets cannot be password protected when uploading Excel layouts to Business Central because Business Central needs to access the data sheets for updates. Password protection is only possible with refreshable Excel reports stored externally on OneDrive or computer.
caveats: only applies to traditional Excel layouts; refreshable reports can be password protected externally

features.name: Excel report layout four-step process
features.description: Creating Excel report layouts follows four steps: get Excel workbook with data contract from Business Central, layout data using Excel features, import layout file back into Business Central, and test the layout.

features.name: Existing report data sets export to Excel
features.description: Any report data set already existing within Business Central can be easily exported to Excel without code required. Custom APIs and report data sets enable building exactly the data needed.

features.name: Excel data analytical capabilities for reporting
features.description: Leveraging Excel's built-in data analytical capabilities such as pivot tables, conditional formatting, and grouping to enhance reporting capabilities and create data-driven reporting experiences from Business Central data.
